# upgradescope server API

<!-- Generated by tools/gen-docs from api/openapi.yaml (make docs-gen). Do not edit. -->

Rendered from the OpenAPI 3.1.0 document [`api/openapi.yaml`](https://github.com/abd-ulbasit/upgradescope/blob/main/api/openapi.yaml), which tests check against every route and handler response.

The REST API of `upgradescope serve`: snapshot ingest from agents, the
read API behind the dashboard, the CI gate, auditor exports and cluster
administration.

**Authentication.** Every credential is a bearer token
(`Authorization: Bearer <token>`). Reads and the gate take the read
token (`serve --read-token`; with none set, they are open), and the
admin token is accepted wherever the read token is. Pushes take the
shared ingest token (`--ingest-token`) or a per-cluster token from
`upgradescope tokens create`. Deleting and renaming clusters take the
admin token (`--admin-token`); without one the server refuses both.
`/healthz` and `/readyz` are never authenticated.

**Errors.** Every error a handler writes is JSON, `{"error": "..."}`,
with a 4xx or 5xx status. An unknown path under `/api/`, or below
`/healthz`, `/readyz`, `/livez` or `/metrics`, is a JSON 404 too. A
known path called with the wrong method gets ServeMux's 405 with an
`Allow` header and a plain-text body. 500 bodies never carry internal
detail: they read `{"error": "internal error"}` and the server logs the
cause.

**Targets** are Kubernetes minors written `MAJOR.MINOR` (`1.38`).
Where a target is optional, the default is the next minor above the
version the cluster's latest snapshot reports.

**Stability.** Paths under `/api/v1` keep their meaning within v1;
fields may be added to responses. See the compatibility policy:
https://abd-ulbasit.github.io/upgradescope/compatibility-policy/

## Authentication

| Scheme | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `readToken` | bearer | `serve --read-token` (or the admin token). Not required when the server runs without one. |
| `ingestToken` | bearer | `serve --ingest-token`, or a per-cluster token from `upgradescope tokens create`. |
| `adminToken` | bearer | `serve --admin-token`. |

## probes

Liveness, readiness and Prometheus metrics.

### `GET /healthz`

**Liveness.** 200 while the process serves; never touches the database.

Auth: none.

| Status | Content type | Schema | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| 200 | `application/json` | [Status](#status) | The process is up. |

### `GET /readyz`

**Readiness.** 200 when the database answers a ping within 2s, else 503.

Auth: none.

| Status | Content type | Schema | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| 200 | `application/json` | [Status](#status) | The database answered. |
| 503 | `application/json` | [Error](#error) | An error. |

### `GET /metrics`

**Prometheus metrics.** Prometheus text exposition: HTTP traffic, ingest results, and per
cluster the score, verdict, blockers, push age and staleness of
its current evaluations. Behind the read token when one is set.
The metric names are listed in the observability reference.

Auth: `readToken` (bearer).

| Status | Content type | Schema | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| 200 | `text/plain` | string | Prometheus text format. |
| 401 | `application/json` | [Error](#error) | An error. |

## ingest

Snapshot pushes from in-cluster agents.

### `POST /api/v1/snapshots`

**Push an inventory snapshot.** What the agent sends every time its cluster's inventory changes and
at least every `--force-sync-every` (1h). The body is JSON,
optionally gzipped (`Content-Encoding: gzip`), at most
`serve --max-snapshot-bytes` (20 MiB) on the wire and after
decompression.

The server stores the inventory as sent and evaluates it against
the cluster's next minor plus `serve --targets`, in one
transaction. A push whose inventory equals the latest stored one
(ignoring `collectedAt` and fields this server does not know) is a
duplicate: 200, nothing new stored. A cluster name is bound to the
`clusterId` (kube-system namespace UID) it first pushed; a push
under that name from another UID, or with none, is a 409.

A per-cluster token may push only as its own cluster (403 before
anything is written).

Auth: `ingestToken` (bearer).

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Content-Encoding` | header | `gzip` \| `identity` | no | — |

Request body (`application/json`): [PushRequest](#pushrequest)

| Status | Content type | Schema | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| 200 | `application/json` | [PushDuplicate](#pushduplicate) | A duplicate of the cluster's latest snapshot. |
| 202 | `application/json` | [PushAccepted](#pushaccepted) | Stored and evaluated. |
| 401 | `application/json` | [Error](#error) | An error. |
| 403 | `application/json` | [Error](#error) | An error. |
| 409 | `application/json` | [Error](#error) | An error. |
| 413 | `application/json` | [Error](#error) | An error. |
| 415 | `application/json` | [Error](#error) | An error. |
| 422 | `application/json` | [Error](#error) | Not judgeable, refused before anything is written: invalid JSON or gzip, an envelope `schemaVersion` other than 1, no `clusterName`, a missing or `null` inventory, an inventory `schemaVersion` other than 1, or a `serverVersion` that is not a Kubernetes 1.x version. |
| 500 | `application/json` | [Error](#error) | An error. |

## fleet

Rollups across every cluster.

### `GET /api/v1/fleet`

**Fleet score matrix.** One row per cluster, one cell per target, from current stored
evaluations only (nothing is recomputed). A cell is `null` when the
cluster has no current evaluation for that target, or already runs
it (then the target is also in the row's `notApplicable`).

Auth: `readToken` (bearer).

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `targets` | query | string | no | Comma-separated minors. Default: every cluster's next minor plus the `serve --targets` minors some cluster does not run yet. |

| Status | Content type | Schema | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| 200 | `application/json` | [FleetResponse](#fleetresponse) | The matrix. |
| 401 | `application/json` | [Error](#error) | An error. |
| 422 | `application/json` | [Error](#error) | An error. |
| 500 | `application/json` | [Error](#error) | An error. |

### `GET /api/v1/fleet/teams`

**Per-team rollup across the fleet.** For one target, each team's worst score, total blockers and the
clusters it has findings in. Each cluster contributes its stored
evaluation, else a what-if from its latest snapshot (`evaluated`
says which); clusters without a snapshot are `missing`, and
clusters that already run the target are `notApplicable`.

Auth: `readToken` (bearer).

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `target` | query | [Target](#target) | yes | — |

| Status | Content type | Schema | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| 200 | `application/json` | [FleetTeamsResponse](#fleetteamsresponse) | The rollup. |
| 401 | `application/json` | [Error](#error) | An error. |
| 422 | `application/json` | [Error](#error) | An error. |
| 500 | `application/json` | [Error](#error) | An error. |

## gate

The CI gate for rendered manifests.

### `POST /api/v1/gate`

**Gate rendered manifests.** Evaluates a YAML (or JSON) manifest stream against a target and
stores nothing. Without `cluster`, the manifests are judged alone,
like `scan --files`. With `cluster`, they are judged inside that
cluster's latest stored inventory (its version, nodes, add-ons and
team labels), and the verdict counts only what the manifests
introduce (findings tagged `source: manifest`); findings the
cluster already has are tagged `source: cluster`.

`fail-on` works like `scan --fail-on` (default `blocker`): when an
introduced finding reaches it, or the verdict is `unknown`, the
status is 422 with the full body, so `curl --fail-with-body` fails
a CI step and keeps the report. `X-Upgradescope-Verdict` always
carries the verdict.

Limits: `serve --max-gate-bytes` (10 MiB) per body, 4 MiB per
document, 20,000 documents. Evaluations run one at a time; a
request that waits more than 30s for its turn, or finds the shared
body budget full, gets 503 with `Retry-After`.

Auth: `readToken` (bearer).

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `target` | query | [Target](#target) | yes | — |
| `cluster` | query | string | no | A cluster name or id whose stored context the manifests are judged in. |
| `format` | query | `json` \| `sarif` | no | — |
| `fail-on` | query | `blocker` \| `warning` \| `never` | no | — |
| `path` | query | string | no | The repository-relative file the stream was rendered to (`deploy/rendered.yaml`). Introduced findings are then located in it in SARIF, so code scanning shows them on the pull request. |

Request body (`application/x-yaml`): string

Request body (`application/json`): string

| Status | Content type | Schema | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| 200 | `application/json` | [GateResponse](#gateresponse) | The gate passed. |
| 200 | `application/sarif+json` | [SARIF](#sarif) | The gate passed. |
| 422 | `application/json` | [GateResponse](#gateresponse) or [Error](#error) | The gate failed (same body as 200), or the request is invalid (no or bad `target`, bad `format`, `fail-on` or `path`, or an undecodable manifest stream: an Error body). |
| 422 | `application/sarif+json` | [SARIF](#sarif) | The gate failed (same body as 200), or the request is invalid (no or bad `target`, bad `format`, `fail-on` or `path`, or an undecodable manifest stream: an Error body). |
| 401 | `application/json` | [Error](#error) | An error. |
| 404 | `application/json` | [Error](#error) | An error. |
| 413 | `application/json` | [Error](#error) | An error. |
| 415 | `application/json` | [Error](#error) | An error. |
| 503 | `application/json` | [Error](#error) | An error. |

## exports

Auditor exports of a stored evaluation.

### `GET /api/v1/clusters/{id}/export`

**Auditor export.** The stored evaluation of the latest snapshot as CSV (one summary
row, one row per finding, one per capability not assessed) or a
self-contained HTML report with the score history. Never a what-if:
404 when no stored evaluation exists for the target, or when the
cluster already runs it.

Auth: `readToken` (bearer).

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | path | integer (int64) | yes | The cluster's numeric id (`id` in the cluster list). A non-integer is a 400. |
| `target` | query | [Target](#target) | no | Target minor. Default, the next minor above the cluster's version. |
| `format` | query | `csv` \| `html` | yes | — |

| Status | Content type | Schema | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| 200 | `text/csv` | string | The export. |
| 200 | `text/html` | string | The export. |
| 400 | `application/json` | [Error](#error) | An error. |
| 401 | `application/json` | [Error](#error) | An error. |
| 404 | `application/json` | [Error](#error) | An error. |
| 422 | `application/json` | [Error](#error) | An error. |

## admin

Cluster administration (admin token).

### `DELETE /api/v1/clusters/{id}`

**Delete a cluster.** Removes the cluster with its snapshots, evaluations, queued
notifications and the per-cluster ingest tokens minted for its
name. An agent still pushing under the name registers it again.

Auth: `adminToken` (bearer).

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | path | integer (int64) | yes | The cluster's numeric id (`id` in the cluster list). A non-integer is a 400. |

| Status | Content type | Schema | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| 204 | — | — | Deleted. |
| 400 | `application/json` | [Error](#error) | An error. |
| 401 | `application/json` | [Error](#error) | An error. |
| 403 | `application/json` | [Error](#error) | No admin token configured, or another token presented. |
| 404 | `application/json` | [Error](#error) | An error. |

### `PATCH /api/v1/clusters/{id}`

**Rename a cluster.** Moves the cluster's history and per-cluster ingest tokens to the new
name. Change the agent's `--cluster-name` too: until then its pushes
under the old name are refused (per-cluster token) or register the
old name again (shared token).

Auth: `adminToken` (bearer).

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | path | integer (int64) | yes | The cluster's numeric id (`id` in the cluster list). A non-integer is a 400. |

Request body (`application/json`): [RenameRequest](#renamerequest)

| Status | Content type | Schema | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| 200 | `application/json` | [Cluster](#cluster) | The renamed cluster. |
| 400 | `application/json` | [Error](#error) | An error. |
| 401 | `application/json` | [Error](#error) | An error. |
| 403 | `application/json` | [Error](#error) | An error. |
| 404 | `application/json` | [Error](#error) | An error. |
| 409 | `application/json` | [Error](#error) | An error. |

| 422 | `application/json` | [Error](#error) | An error. |

## Schemas

### Error

Every error a handler writes.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `error` | string | yes | — |

### Status

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `status` | `ok` | yes | — |

### Target

A Kubernetes minor, `MAJOR.MINOR`.

Type: string, pattern `^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$`.

### Verdict

`blocked`: at least one blocker. `unknown`: no blocker found, but a
required check was not assessed, so one may have been missed.
`ready`: neither.

Type: `ready`, `blocked`, `unknown`.

### Severity

Type: `blocker`, `warning`, `info`.

### Category

One of `removed-api`, `deprecated-api`, `deprecated-api-in-use`,
`eol-addon`, `eol-approaching`, `version-skew`, `chart-incompat`,
`kb-stale`, `addon-no-data`, `unknown-api`. A release may add
categories under `/api/v1`, so this is not an enum: treat one you do
not know by its severity.

Type: string.
